passages.title: Balancing Remote Work
passages.text: Working from home saves travel time, although it can make teamwork harder. A flexible schedule may offer a better balance, provided everyone agrees on how to stay in touch.
passages.levelRationale: The passage weighs competing effects and adds a condition to its recommendation.

passages.title: Managing Popular Places
passages.text: Tourism supports local businesses, yet large crowds can damage the places visitors came to enjoy. Limiting daily entry might protect the area while preserving most of its economic benefits.
passages.levelRationale: A public issue is evaluated through contrast, consequences, and a qualified solution.

passages.title: Changing Sleep Habits
passages.text: People often blame a busy schedule for poor sleep, but evening habits may be equally important. Reducing bright screens before bed is a modest change that can make rest more consistent.
passages.levelRationale: The text challenges a common explanation and advances a measured alternative claim.

passages.title: Trees in Growing Cities
passages.text: Planting trees can cool crowded neighborhoods and improve air quality, but young trees require years of care. Cities should therefore fund maintenance as seriously as they fund the initial planting.
passages.levelRationale: A policy recommendation follows from balanced environmental benefits and practical constraints.

passages.title: Keeping Paper Tickets
passages.text: Digital tickets are convenient for most travelers, but a phone can fail at the worst moment. Transport companies should retain a simple paper option for passengers who need it.
passages.levelRationale: The passage balances convenience against reliability and makes a qualified service recommendation.

passages.title: The Value of Shared Meals
passages.text: Shared meals do not automatically create close relationships, yet they offer people regular time to listen. Even one unhurried dinner each week can strengthen a family's sense of connection.
passages.levelRationale: A measured claim acknowledges a limitation before supporting a broader social benefit.
